app.title: The honest SPHEREx comparator
app.tagline: Every frame with its real λ. Every visit, a coadd. Every subtraction, a verdict.

home.asteroids: Asteroids (the only thing that visibly moves)
home.thesis: SPHEREx images the whole sky in 102 infrared colours, but every pixel sees a different colour: a naive ‘before and after’ lies. Here every frame shows its real λ, every visit collapses into a variance-weighted coadd, every subtraction passes a spectral verdict, and every point is cross-matched with Gaia DR3, CatWISE2020, AllWISE, SIMBAD and known asteroids. We do not promise to find Planet X: what cannot be seen, we state with numbers.
home.heroA: Every frame with its real λ.
home.limitsText: Parallax, Planet Nine and saturation have figures measured on real coadds. What SPHEREx cannot see, we say before you go looking.
home.proofResidualSub: measured on 153 real pairs; 25 % at 16 channels

classroom.pixel: A SPHEREx pixel is 6.15″: a star with a proper motion of 10″/yr moves less than 2 pixels per year.
classroom.visit: A visit is a set of exposures less than 1 day apart: this one has {n}, from {lo} to {hi} µm. Within a visit each exposure sees a different colour (λ ladder), not a different epoch.
classroom.motion: This object moves {arcsec}″/yr = {px} px/yr: {total} px in {years} years. Hence the visit coadd and the 2010 reference.
classroom.noMotion: This field has no known proper-motion object: whatever changes between visits is brightness (variability), colour (λ) or a passing asteroid.
classroom.verdictRule: Subtracting two frames is only valid at the same λ: ≤ 2 channels OK, 3–8 warning, > 8 blocked (measured residual: 4 % + 1.4 %/channel).
classroom.saturation: Magenta pixels are saturated (OVERFLOW/BLOOM): they are shown and counted, never hidden.
classroom.known: Click any point to ask “what is here?” to Gaia, CatWISE, AllWISE, SIMBAD and JPL.
classroom.tryIt: Try: ← → to change visit; ↑ ↓ to walk the λ ladder; A − B mode to see the verdict.

limits.title: Limits & Method
limits.intro: Everything this viewer claims is measured on real SPHEREx data (QR3/DR1) and stated here with numbers and sources: what can be seen, what cannot, and why. Values are regenerated by scripts/limits_analysis.py.
limits.missing: limits.json has not been generated yet.

method.title: Method
method.s1: Exposures per position via the IRSA TAP (spherex.plane ⋈ spherex.artifact; release from obs_publisher_did).
method.s2: Cutout by HTTP Range on the public bucket s3://nasa-irsa-spherex (IMAGE, FLAGS, VARIANCE, ZODI, WCS-WAVE; ~2 MB per exposure; DR1 Rice-compressed FLAGS decompressed by rows). Fallback: IRSA cutout service.
method.s3: IMAGE − ZODI; fatal pixels filled from neighbours before reprojection (display) and masked afterwards (photometry); OVERFLOW/BLOOM are painted, never hidden. λ of each exposure from the spectral WCS “W”.
method.s4: Reprojection onto a common north-up TAN grid at 6.15″/px; visit = exposures less than 1 day apart; 1/VARIANCE-weighted coadd.
method.s5: Aperture photometry r = 2.5 px, annulus 5–8 px, recentred per visit, µJy via the solid-angle map (F = I·Ω·23.504).
method.s6: A−B only after the spectral verdict; cross-match with Gaia DR3 (propagated), CatWISE2020, AllWISE, SIMBAD and JPL sb_ident with the SPHEREx state vector.

dl.title: Subtraction residual vs Δλ
dl.intro: The background subtracts cleanly (RMS/noise 0.80–0.87: the pipeline VARIANCE is honest). Stars do not: a {floor} % floor from resampling plus {slope} % per channel of separation (Rayleigh-Jeans predicts {rj} %/channel). Hence the rule ok ≤ 2 / warn 3–8 / block > 8 channels.

pm.title: Measured proper motion vs catalogue
pm.intro: Linear fit to the per-visit (coadd) centroids of the showcase; the error is the fit error. Direction: x grows westwards.
pm.note: WISE 0855 and ε Indi B are measured; Barnard saturates its core in D2–D3 and its (wing) centroid is biased: shown anyway, with a warning.
pm.controlNote: Control: the same fit applied to Gaia field stars (G < 16, away from the object) after removing their catalogue pm; their residual |pm| is the systematic floor of the method.

inj.title: Injection–recovery on real coadds
inj.intro: Synthetic sources with a Gaussian PSF (header PSF_FWHM = {fwhm}″) injected at source-free positions of three real coadds; recovered if S/N ≥ 5 in the aperture and the centroid lands within 1 px.

fg.title: Field Guide: SPHEREx artefacts in real cutouts
fg.intro: Each cutout is a real exposure (0.1°, ×6) with the corresponding FLAGS bit painted. Before reporting a “candidate”, compare with these.
fg.openDiff: Open the > 8-channel subtraction in the viewer

saturation.title: Saturation and BLOOM
saturation.alt: Saturated core of a bright star with charge bleeding
saturation.text: OVERFLOW (bit 1) and BLOOM (bit 26): the core is NaN and charge bleeds along columns. R Dra and RW Aur saturate in every exposure; aperture photometry is meaningless.

dichroic.title: Dichroic edge
dichroic.text: Bit 7: dichroic region where the response drops; appears as a stripe. Not a source.

snowball.title: Snowball
snowball.alt: Compact group of pixels flagged SNOWBALL
snowball.text: Bit 27: high-energy particle event with a halo; appears in ONE exposure and does not repeat along the λ ladder.

streak.title: Streak
streak.text: Bit 25: satellite or debris crossing the exposure; linear, single exposure.

persist.title: Persistence
persist.alt: Pixels flagged PERSIST after a bright source
persist.text: Bit 17: latent image of a bright source from the previous exposure; can mimic a faint source that “moves” with the scan pattern.

ghost.title: Ghost
ghost.text: Bit 22: internal reflection of a bright source.

lambda_dipole.title: λ dipole
lambda_dipole.alt: Difference of two exposures at different λ
lambda_dipole.text: Subtracting exposures more than 8 channels apart leaves 15–25 % dipole-shaped residuals on stars: not motion, colour + resampling. The viewer blocks that subtraction.

vel.title: Completeness by velocity (synthetic movers)
vel.intro: Synthetic movers injected into the real coadds of {n} visits of WISE 0855 D5 ({span} yr) and recovered blind: centroid within ±3 px of the initial position in every visit plus a linear fit. Recovered if the fitted pm is within 30 % (or 0.3 px/yr) of the injected one.
vel.note: The drop at high pm is the limit of the per-visit method without a known pm: the object leaves the search box. With a catalogue pm (Gaia, CatWISE) the position is propagated and the limit disappears; without it, above ~2 px/yr (12″/yr) detections must be linked, not centroided.

changes.title: Changes at the same λ
changes.method: Each exposure is subtracted from the median of same-channel exposures in other visits (|Δ| = 0 channels, verdict ok by construction). Peaks with S/N ≥ 6 and ≥ 2 px, away from saturation, cross-matched with Gaia, CatWISE, AllWISE, SIMBAD and JPL.
changes.empty: No changes with S/N ≥ 6 in this detector.
changes.none: No precomputed list for this field.
changes.single: single exposure: possible artefact (cosmic ray, snowball, persistence)
changes.caveat: Not a Planet X detector. A filter of “what changed at the same λ”: variability of known sources, asteroids and artefacts. A real candidate must repeat across exposures and not be in the Field Guide.
